To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrophoretic mobilities of DNA in agarose gels at low electric field strength can be predicted by the extended LDZ equation.
the electrophoretic migration of a DNA molecule in a gel is determined by a combination of the reptation and size-exclusion mechanisms.

the electrophoretic mobilities of DNA fragments of different lengths are not linearly dependent on the inverse square root of the chain lengths, but rather are nonlinearly dependent on the reciprocal chain lengths at low electric field strength, and the electrophoretically observed chain lengths of DNA fragments are smaller than their true lengths, and this size discrepancy is not accounted for in reptation models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the theory of the gel electrophoretic separation of DNA.
the theory of gel-electrophoresis of linear polymers.
a theoretical description of the electrophoretic migration of DNA molecules in agarose gels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
reptation alone cannot explain all aspects of gel electrophoretic mobilities of DNA.
reptation is the dominant mechanism for DNA electrophoresis at low electric field strength and that size-exclusion effects become important at high electric field strength.
the present model, which is a natural extension of the LDZ theory, is consistent with all the experimental data that have been reported to date.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present model provides a good fit of the observed mobility data over a broad range of chain length and electric field strength.
the reptation model for the gel-electrophoretic behavior of DNA molecules is a useful approximation, but that the theory needs to be extended and evaluated.

the reptation mechanism, as described in the present work, is the dominant mechanism at low electric field, and the observed nonlinear variation in mu with 1/Lc is due to the correlation of segment-to-field angles in the force-balance expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reptating wormlike chain model is the most appropriate for describing gel electrophoreses of DNA.
the reptation model, as originally formulated by Lumpkin, DèJardin, and Zimm (LDZ), is a good model for the gel-electrophoretic behavior of DNA, but that it must be modified for finite chain length.
the present theory, in combination with the experimental data, provides a more complete understanding of the physics of DNA electrophoresis.
